To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a panel of mAb's to NS1 of MVE were used to identify the most appropriate antibody for affinity chromatography.

a combination of immunoaffinity chromatography with a novel approach to selecting the optimal elution conditions has been successfully used to purify the non-structural protein NS1 of Murray Valley encepalitis virus.
the appropriate ligands and optimal conditions can be rapidly and easily determined for immunoaffnity purification of proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to select the most appropriate ligand for affinity purification of a viral antigen and to determine optimal conditions for elusion.
the development of immunoassays for the detection of flavivirus infections and the purification of the NS-1 protein of Murray valley encephalitis and Kunjin viruses.
the development of a rapid and efficient immunoaffinity procedure for purification of a viral protein, the non-structural protein NS1 of Murray Valley encepalitis virus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NS1 protein can be purified in good yield by immunoaffinity chromatography using the selected mAb and elution conditions.
the NS1 protein was purified from crude cell lysate by immunoaffinity chromatography on mAb-sephrose columns using a pH 11.0-11.5 buffer as the elution agent.
the NS1 protein is a promising target for the development of a vaccine against MVE virus, as well as other flaviviruses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a panel of monoclonal antibodies and ELISA to determine the appropriate ligand (antibody) and elution buffer for affinity chromatography of a protein antigen is a rapid and reliable method.
immunoaffinity columns can be constructed using a variety of antibodies and elution conditions.

immunoaffinity chromatography using mAbs is a useful tool for rapid purification of proteins, but that the choice of the most suitable antibody and elution conditions is critical to the success of the procedure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

immunoaffinity chromatography can be used for purification of a wide range of antigens, provided that the appropriate antibody is used, the conditions of binding are optimised and the appropriate conditions for elution of the antigen are determined.
the optimal conditions for eluting an antigen from an immunoaffinity column are likely to be very similar to those required for dissociation of the antigen-antibody complex in solution.

the optimal conditions for eluting an antigen from a ligand can be determined by ELISA in microtitre plates, and that these conditions are likely to be similar to those used for eluting antigen from a liganded solid phase.
